q: In the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz, what color are the magic slippers Dorothy wears?
note: They were silver in L. Frank Baum's novel, and MGM switched them to ruby to show off Technicolor.

q: In the 1977 film Star Wars, what is the name of Han Solo's battered freighter?
note: Han brags that it made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs, a boast about distance rather than time.

q: In the 1960 thriller Psycho, where in the Bates Motel is Marion Crane murdered?
note: Bernard Herrmann scored the entire film for string instruments alone, including those shrieking violins.

q: In the 1985 film Back to the Future, what make of car does Doc Brown turn into a time machine?
note: The car has to hit 88 miles per hour and draw 1.21 gigawatts of power to jump through time.

q: What is the dying word spoken in the opening scene of the 1941 film Citizen Kane?
note: Orson Welles co-wrote, directed and starred in the picture, his first feature film.

q: Which actress played the singing governess Maria in the 1965 film The Sound of Music?
note: She won the Best Actress Oscar for Mary Poppins, released the year before.

q: In the 1975 film Jaws, what is the name of the beach town terrorized by the great white shark?
note: The mechanical shark broke down so often that the director kept it hidden, which only made the film scarier.

q: Which actor played the aging Don Vito Corleone in the 1972 film The Godfather?
note: He won Best Actor for the role and refused the award in protest at Hollywood's portrayal of Native Americans.

q: What is the name of the ship's computer that turns on the crew in the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey?
note: Each letter of HAL sits one place before IBM in the alphabet, which Arthur C. Clarke always insisted was a coincidence.

q: In the 1982 film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, what brand of candy does Elliott use to coax E.T. into his house?
note: Mars turned down the chance to use M&M's, and sales of Reese's Pieces soared after the film opened.

q: In the 1939 epic Gone with the Wind, what is the name of Scarlett O'Hara's family plantation?
note: Hattie McDaniel won Best Supporting Actress for the film, the first Academy Award given to a Black performer.

q: What is the name of the snowbound Colorado hotel in the 1980 film The Shining?
note: Stephen King disliked Kubrick's version so much that he backed a more faithful television remake in 1997.

q: Which heavyweight champion does Rocky Balboa fight in the climax of the 1976 film Rocky?
note: Sylvester Stallone wrote the screenplay himself and refused to sell it unless he could star in it.

q: Which 1979 science fiction film introduced Sigourney Weaver as Warrant Officer Ripley?
note: Ridley Scott kept the cast in the dark about the chestburster scene, so much of their horror is genuine.

q: What is the name of the nightclub run by Humphrey Bogart's character in the 1942 film Casablanca?
note: The film's most quoted line, 'Play it again, Sam,' is never actually spoken in it.

q: Which star sings and dances the title number through a downpour in the 1952 musical Singin' in the Rain?
note: The story is set during Hollywood's chaotic switch from silent pictures to talkies.

q: Which actor played T. E. Lawrence in the 1962 epic Lawrence of Arabia?
note: He was nominated for eight acting Oscars across his career and never won a competitive one.

q: How many different roles did Peter Sellers play in the 1964 satire Dr. Strangelove?
note: He was meant to play a fourth, the bomber pilot, but an injury handed that part to Slim Pickens.

q: Which 1974 Roman Polanski film about Los Angeles water rights ends with the line 'Forget it, Jake. It's Chinatown'?
note: Screenwriter Robert Towne took home the film's only Academy Award.

q: Which 1959 Billy Wilder comedy closes with the line 'Nobody's perfect'?
note: Joe E. Brown delivers it after learning that his fiancée is a man in disguise.
